request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have a to-date, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The server and the screen each look up rates in one place: `RateRepository.find` on the server and `rateFor` in `rates.ts` on the screen. I changed both the same way. When the rate that would apply to a claim has a to-date before the claim's date, the lookup now returns no rate. Everything that reads due works from that lookup, so it all follows without separate changes: claim due shows n/a, person and sheet totals skip it, a statement binds n/a, the late charge adds nothing, and the current rate for today can be n/a too.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V26__rate_to.sql`, adds a nullable `to_date` column to the rate table.
- **Server:**
  - Rate requests, responses and stored rates now carry `to`.
  - A to-date before the from-date is refused with a 400 and writes nothing.
  - The `RATE_SET` audit line ends with ` to=<date>` when a to-date is given.
- **Screen:** the rate form has a To field (`rate-form-to`), and each rate row shows its to-date (`rate-to`). I also reworded the form's error message to mention the date rules.

A rate without a from-date still applies from the beginning of time, as it did before. The test expects this.
